title: Spotting between periods
answer: Spotting means light bleeding or brown marks between periods, needing only a liner or none. It can happen in the first years of periods, around ovulation, with some contraceptive methods, or from stress. But it can also be a sign of infection or another problem, especially if it happens often, after sex, or with pain, bad-smelling discharge or fever. If spotting keeps happening, see a health worker at your health center.
